long.account: The main screen after sign-in. Shows live metrics (engagements, controls, frameworks), the 6-step onboarding progress and quick access to key sections. New users are offered the interactive tour from here. Full navigation is always on the left.
long.dashboard: Group-wide summary panels: open and total findings, engagement and subsidiary counts. Data is split by level — the whole group and each subsidiary, plus a per-department view. Use it as the daily starting point: if open findings grow, drill into the engagement behind them.
long.dashboards: A chart builder that needs no developer: create a dashboard, add widgets (bar, line, pie) over chosen audit metrics. Widgets recompute automatically on every open. Handy for management-meeting visuals.
long.reports: Produce finished audit documents: a full PDF report (for the regulator and management), Word (for edits) and Excel (for analysis). The report captures the checklist, answers, findings and statuses at generation time, in the languages the client requires (EN/AZ/RU).
long.snapshots: Freeze the full compliance state at a date: how many controls pass, which findings are open. Snapshots are immutable — your evidence of "how it was". Comparing two snapshots shows the diff: what improved and what degraded. Take one before and after major changes.
long.trends: Metric dynamics between snapshots: for every metric the first and last value, the delta and the direction (up/down/flat), grouped by metric type. It answers management's question "are we getting better or worse?" — with numbers.
long.kpi: Numeric key indicators for controls: set a target (e.g. "vulnerability closure time ≤ 30 days"), a direction (higher or lower is better) and a period. Record measurements — the platform computes the on-track status direction-aware. KPIs make control effectiveness measurable.
long.frameworks: The library of standards you audit against. Global ones ship out of the box (ISO 27001, COBIT, NIST, CBAR — the local regulator requirement) and are versioned (published/draft/deprecated); your own frameworks are added at tenant level. Controls map to standard clauses — that is how coverage is built.
long.controls: The control catalog — the foundation of every audit. The global library provides ready controls with audit-question wording; for your specifics a control is "adapted" — a tenant version with changed wording is created without touching the original. A control carries its change history, team comments and attached tests with statuses (ok/failing/needs attention).
long.policies: The register of internal policies (security, password, access, etc.) with versioning: upload a document, publish a new version — the old ones are kept. Employee acknowledgement is tracked — who read it and when. At audit time this is ready evidence that policies exist and are current.
long.commitments: The register of obligations taken in customer contracts: SLA, uptime, support terms. Each commitment has a status (met / at risk / breached) and an SLA indicator (ok / due soon / overdue). So you never learn about a breached contract from the customer.
long.universe: The audit universe — a map of everything auditable: systems, processes, units. Each entity links to the audits performed — coverage and never-audited "white spots" become visible at once. The basis of risk-based planning.
long.engagements: The central section — the audits themselves. Lifecycle via a state machine: draft → manager review → issued to respondents → responses → findings drafting → management response → approval → report issued → follow-up → closed (plus pause and archive). The checklist is built from library controls as snapshots; respondents answer with compliance statuses; the platform suggests draft findings for the gaps. Plan/actual milestones, engagement export and duplicate/restore included.
long.audit-programs: Audit templates: a set of controls assembled once is applied to new audits in one click — no need to rebuild the checklist every year. Programs mature with your audit function: extend them after every cycle.
long.working-papers: The auditor's working papers — a formalized trail of the work. A paper moves through statuses (draft → review → signed); the signature is attributed (who and in which role) and post-review edits are flagged automatically. Inside: three annotation types — comment, tick mark and exception; an exception report is built per engagement.
long.plans: Annual planning: which audits, in which subsidiaries, in which periods. Plan versus actual shows the slippage. This is the document a regulator asks for first.
long.allocations: Auditor allocation across engagements with planned hours. Everyone's workload is visible — who is overloaded and who has capacity. Use it when planning a new audit so it does not land on busy people.
long.time: Actual hours per engagement. Comparing actuals with the audit's hour budget reveals overruns before they become a problem. The data feeds internal reporting and audit costing.
long.satisfaction: Auditee satisfaction surveys after an audit closes: scores and comments. Systematic feedback improves the process and demonstrates the audit function's quality to management.
long.risks: The risk register: every risk is scored by likelihood and impact, gets an owner and a treatment plan. Risks link to controls — you see exactly what mitigates each risk. The register feeds risk-based audit planning.
long.risk-heatmap: The 5×5 heat map: all risks on one likelihood × impact matrix. The red zone is what needs attention now. Clicking a cell opens the risks in it. The best slide for a risk briefing.
long.privacy: The GDPR block in two parts. ROPA (Art. 30 register of processing activities): each activity carries a legal basis (consent/contract/legal obligation, etc.), data and subject categories, recipients, retention and a cross-border flag; role — controller/processor/joint. DPIA (impact assessment): for risky activities — risk level, mitigations, a workflow to completion and attached documents.
long.iam: Accounts from your systems in one place: owner, MFA status, privileged flag. The basis for checks like "does everyone have MFA" and "who holds admin rights". Data arrives via import or connectors.
long.access-reviews: Access recertification campaigns: launch a campaign per system, reviewers decide keep or revoke for every account. Outcomes are recorded. Regular campaigns are a direct requirement of most security standards.
long.devices: Endpoint compliance: disk encryption, antivirus, screen lock. Non-compliant devices are visible immediately and sent for remediation. At audit time — ready evidence of endpoint control.
long.security-alerts: Incoming security events in one queue: triage by severity, assign, close with a resolution. The alert-handling history is evidence of a working response process.
long.vulnerabilities: The vulnerability register: source (scanner, pentest, bug bounty), severity and remediation SLA. Overdue ones are highlighted. Closure requires verification. Shows the regulator a managed vulnerability process.
long.code-changes: The log of code and configuration changes (change management): what changed, who approved, when it shipped. Linking a change to its approval is a classic ITGC requirement. Filled manually or via connectors.
long.vendors: Third-party risk management: a vendor register, assessment questionnaires, recorded risk level and status. Critical vendors get regular reassessment. An ISO 27001 (A.15) requirement and a regulator focus.
long.trust-center: Your public compliance page: which certifications and controls are in place — for customers and partners without NDA email threads. You choose what to show; the link goes to the customer.
long.questionnaires: Inbound security questionnaires from your customers (their vendor check on you). Answers are filled with knowledge-base reuse — an answer written once is reused. The sending history is kept.
long.knowledge-base: The base of ready answers (Q&A) for questionnaires and recurring customer questions. It grows as you work; outdated answers get refreshed. The fuller the base, the faster questionnaires close.
long.personnel: The employee register with lifecycle: joining (an onboarding checklist — access, training, policies) and leaving (offboarding — access revocation, equipment return). Unfinished steps stay visible. The control most often tested in security audits.
long.connectors: Integrations with external systems for automatic data collection (accounts, devices, vulnerabilities). Credentials are stored encrypted only (AES-256-GCM). A connected source turns manual checks into automatic ones.
long.config: Tenant settings: reference lists (audit types, custom lists, custom fields) with full change history — who changed what, with rollback to prior versions. Config export/import moves the setup between installations.
long.field-permissions: Fine-grained permissions on top of roles: for a given role hide a field entirely, make it read-only or allow editing (e.g. hide finding recommendations from the Collaborator role). Enforced at the API level — it cannot be bypassed through the UI.
long.api-keys: Programmatic access to the platform: create a key (shown once, stored as a hash), call the REST API with the X-Api-Key header. Full OpenAPI documentation lives at /docs on the API server. Keys revoke instantly.
long.notifications: Notification rules — which events send emails (finding deadlines, assignments, status changes) — and a log of everything sent. Noise is switched off per rule.
long.migration: Historical data migration: upload a past-years Excel checklist, the platform parses the structure (preview before import) and creates controls with domains in your library. The import is idempotent — re-uploading creates no duplicates.
long.ai-settings: Plug in an AI assistant of your choice: Anthropic Claude, any OpenAI-compatible provider (GPT, Kimi, DeepSeek) or a local model inside your perimeter (Ollama/vLLM) — then data never leaves your infrastructure. The key is stored encrypted and never shown again. Without AI, all assist features run in deterministic mode.
long.glossary: A shared GRC glossary (control, finding, RCM, DPIA, ROPA…) with localization. Extend it with your own terms — the team and auditees speak one language.
long.guide: The help center: every section described with usage steps, an interactive UI tour and this reference. The “?” button in the header opens help for the section you are in.
long.my-work: My Work gathers everything assigned to you across the platform: findings you own, tests you maintain, policies awaiting your approval, policies to attest and your access requests. Employees land here after login.
long.findings: The findings register lists every finding across audits with risk, status and SLA. Open a finding to assign an owner, move it through its lifecycle and re-test before closing; comments and history live on the card.
long.documents: Documents are manual evidence. Upload a file, link it to a control or engagement, set a renew-by date and reassign the owner. Downloads are authorized and byte-exact.
long.tests: Tests verify controls continuously. The registry shows status, SLA and owner; the card holds run history with failing entities and evidence. Automated tests can be run on demand; stale tests can be deactivated.
long.roles: Roles define the resource×action permission matrix. System presets are read-only; create custom tenant roles and set matrix cells to none/view/edit.
long.members: Members lists everyone in the tenant with email, category (auditor / end user / MSP) and role. Change a member’s role inline — the change is journaled.
long.assets: The asset inventory lists every IT asset in scope — ERP systems, databases, network devices, applications, cloud services and endpoints. Each asset shows its owner and where it came from: created manually or discovered automatically through a connector. Assets can be tagged in bulk (e.g. to mark PCI or SOX scope) and the whole inventory exports to CSV for auditors. Assets are projected into the Audit Universe, so risks can be linked to them.
long.roadmap: The roadmap turns each activated framework into a phased implementation plan — Setup, Policies, Remediation, Audit — with progress computed from live data (control coverage, approved policies, closed findings, passing tests). Set an audit-ready target date and the roadmap flags whether you are on or off track. Use it to see, at a glance, how close each standard is to being audit-ready.
long.sso-settings: Configure single sign-on for this tenant: choose OIDC or SAML, set the email domain, issuer/metadata URL, client ID and secret. The secret is stored encrypted and never shown again. Use this when your organization runs its own identity provider and wants employees to sign in with corporate credentials.
long.security: Personal security settings. Enable two-factor authentication (2FA): scan a QR with an authenticator app, confirm a code, and save one-time recovery codes. Disabling requires a current code. 2FA adds a second step at sign-in on top of your password or magic link.
long.auditors: Invite external auditors by email, scope them to specific subsidiaries, set a time-boxed access window, and revoke access. Also lists internal members and MSPs by category.
long.auditor-view: The auditor storefront for a selected audit: review evidence with statuses, record auditor assessments with rounds, and request documents from the client (PBC).

compliance.d: Frameworks (ISO/COBIT/NIST), the controls library, policies and commitments.

engagements.d: The heart of the platform: audits with checklists, working papers, plans and time tracking.

risk.d: Risk register, heat map and GDPR (ROPA/DPIA).

security.d: Accounts, access reviews, devices, vulnerabilities and changes.

thirdParty.d: Vendor risk, Trust Center, questionnaires and the knowledge base.

org.d: People, integrations, permissions, Excel import and the AI provider.

breadcrumbs.d: Always know where you are. The home icon returns to the main screen.

profile.d: Your account and the sign-out button live at the bottom of the panel.

findings.title: Findings
findings.aiControlClauseFallback: Control clause is inherited from the linked checklist item.
findings.aiReasoningFallback: The finding was created from an AI draft after human acceptance.
findings.aiRiskJustificationFallback: Initial risk is {risk} based on the observed control gap and available evidence.
findings.templatesHint: Common findings with preset risk and recommendation — one click creates an identified finding you can edit.

documents.title: Documents
documents.uploadContextBody: The form has already selected the target: {target}. After upload, the file will land in that evidence pool.
documents.auditFirmsHint: External auditors invited to review evidence.
documents.requestHint: Create a placeholder for a document you expect but do not have yet.

intake.title: Document readiness for AI analysis
intake.subtitle: Shows which formats are already collected, what can support draft findings, and where OCR, upload or control/audit linking is still needed.
intake.formatsSubtitle: PDF, Word, Excel, CSV, images and technical config/log files are routed into extraction, OCR and evidence-backed draft finding queues.

spreadsheet.label: Excel / CSV
spreadsheet.hint: Registers, exports, access matrices and lists

imageOcr.label: Scans / OCR
imageOcr.hint: Images and scanned evidence that need OCR

configLogs.label: Configs / logs
configLogs.hint: Technical exports, logs and machine-readable files

linked.label: Evidence-grounded
linked.hint: Active linked documents are the base for evidence-backed AI drafts

ocr.label: OCR queue
ocr.hint: Scanned evidence needs recognition before analysis

blocked.label: Analysis blockers
blocked.hint: Expected or unlinked documents are not ready for AI review yet

rescan.title: What new evidence will refresh next
rescan.subtitle: A read-only plan for the last {days} days: evidence extraction, OCR, AI finding drafts, request follow-up and report readiness.

extraction.label: Extraction
extraction.hint: Active linked files ready for parsing

evidenceRequestFollowUp.label: PBC follow-up
evidenceRequestFollowUp.hint: Requests and drafts blocking the queue

reportReadinessRefresh.label: Reports
reportReadinessRefresh.hint: Accepted or ready evidence feeding deliverables

rescan.triggerGate: AI output stays draft-only until auditor review

triggerReasons.linked_evidence_upload: Linked evidence starts the re-scan chain
triggerReasons.draft_review_gate: Draft evidence waits for review before re-scan
triggerReasons.link_required: Link this evidence before AI refresh

rescan.noTriggers: No recent document changes in the re-scan window.

readiness.title: Evidence readiness
readiness.subtitle: A board-level view of collected evidence, links, auditor review and renewal gaps before reporting starts.
readiness.signalBody: The score favors active, linked, accepted evidence and penalizes flagged, expired or orphaned documents.

search.title: Search
search.hint: Type a query in the top bar — findings, controls, documents, working papers, knowledge base and audit programs are searched.
search.askEmpty: No matching findings or evidence documents

myWork.title: My work
myWork.allDone: Nothing assigned to you — all clear.

assets.title: Asset Inventory
assets.name: Name
assets.bulkHint: Check assets in the table, enter a tag name, apply.

roadmap.title: Roadmap
roadmap.empty: Activate a framework to build its roadmap.

coverage.title: Requirements traceability map
coverage.subtitle: Key requirement chapters are tied to live platform modules so clients see a covered audit workflow, not a loose set of screens.

workflow.title: Audit engine and progress
workflow.hint: Audit charter, phases, control statuses, domains and progress by test work.

riskRegister.title: Single risk register
riskRegister.hint: Manual and AI-proposed risks with business impact categories, affected process/asset context and human approval.

documentAi.title: AI document analysis and findings
documentAi.hint: Finding drafts are evidence-grounded and explainable; intake and rescan planning show PDF/Office, spreadsheets, configs and the OCR queue.

recommendations.title: Recommendations and action plan
recommendations.hint: Findings turn into remediation tasks with owners and due dates.

deliverables.title: Standard document package
deliverables.hint: Audit Report, Non-Conformities, Risk Matrix, Action Plan and Executive Summary in PDF/Word/Excel.

trustSecurity.title: Trust, security and privacy
trustSecurity.hint: RBAC, tenant isolation, private deployment, immutable audit log, AI traceability and guardrails.

collaboration.title: Collaboration and evidence workflow
collaboration.hint: Audit team, tasks, DRL, evidence requests and review statuses.

integrations.title: Integrations and mapping
integrations.hint: REST API, connectors and cross-framework mapping for reusable controls.

reportingUx.title: Reporting and multilingual UX
reportingUx.hint: Dashboards, scheduled report delivery plan, wired email digest worker and RU/AZ/EN interface.

advancedAi.title: Advanced AI loop
advancedAi.hint: Conversational search, auto-DRL, evidence rescan planning, continuous monitoring and auditor review gates are live.

trustPublic.requestHint: Request access to detailed documentation. We will review and grant a private link.
trustPublic.sent: Request sent — you will hear from us by email.
trustPublic.notFound: This Trust Center is not available.

ssoSettings.title: SSO (Single Sign-On)
ssoSettings.intro: Connect your organization's own identity provider (OIDC or SAML) for this tenant.
ssoSettings.emailDomainHint: Users with this email domain are routed to your IdP.
ssoSettings.entryPointHint: OIDC issuer or SAML metadata / entry-point URL.
ssoSettings.secretHint: Stored encrypted; never shown again. Leave blank to keep.
ssoSettings.note: Login-flow routing to per-tenant IdPs is applied by the auth layer; configuration is stored here.

security.title: Security
security.enabledDesc: 2FA is enabled — a one-time code is required at sign-in.
security.offDesc: Add a second factor: an authenticator app generates a one-time code at sign-in.
security.scanHint: Scan this QR in your authenticator app (Google Authenticator, Authy…), then enter the 6-digit code.
security.recoveryHint: Save these recovery codes somewhere safe — each works once if you lose your device. Shown only now.
security.requiredBody: Enable two-factor authentication below to comply with your organization policy.

auditors.title: Auditors
auditors.subtitle: Invite external auditors, scope them to subsidiaries, set access windows, and revoke access.
auditors.scopeHint: Leave empty to grant access to the whole group.
auditors.name: Name

auditorView.title: Auditor view
auditorView.subtitle: Review evidence, record assessments, and request documents from the client for an audit.
